experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment tests the hypothesis that high-resolution temporal monitoring of bacterial metabolic states can identify transient windows of susceptibility in multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains. The core technical challenge is synchronizing real-time metabolic flux data (e.g., NADH/NAD+ ratios, ATP levels, membrane potential) with antibiotic exposure timing. We will employ microfluidic biosensors capable of sub-minute resolution metabolic profiling, coupled with automated drug delivery systems. The study focuses on correlating specific metabolic 'signatures' (defined as deviations from homeostatic baseline >2 SD) with subsequent bacterial survival rates upon antibiotic challenge. The mechanism posits that resistance is not always constitutive but may have dynamic metabolic costs that create temporary vulnerabilities.

source.description: Synthetic/Experimental dataset generated during this study. It includes time-stamped metabolic markers (fluorescence/intensity readings from biosensors) for E. coli and S. aureus MDR strains under controlled growth conditions.

target.access_note: Derived from parallel viability assays (CFU counting) synchronized with metabolic monitoring.

experiment_design.methods: 1. Strain Selection: Use 5 clinically relevant MDR strains (e.g., ESBL-producing E. coli, MRSA). 2. Biosensor Setup: Implement microfluidic chips with integrated optical sensors for real-time monitoring of metabolic indicators (NADH autofluorescence, membrane potential dyes). 3. Dynamic Exposure Protocol: Expose cultures to sub-lethal and lethal doses of standard antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, vancomycin) at randomized time points relative to metabolic cycles. 4. Data Acquisition: Record metabolic data at 10-second intervals. 5. Viability Assay: Perform colony-forming unit (CFU) counts at T+0, T+1h, T+4h, T+24h post-exposure to determine survival. 6. Correlation Analysis: Use time-lagged cross-correlation and machine learning (Random Forest/LSTM) to identify metabolic features preceding susceptibility windows.

baselines: Standard MIC Testing: Conventional broth microdilution to establish baseline static resistance profiles.
Random Timing Control: Antibiotic administration at random time points without metabolic guidance to establish average efficacy.
Constitutive Resistance Model: A null model assuming no temporal variation in susceptibility, predicting constant survival rates regardless of metabolic state.
metrics: Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC): To evaluate the classifier's ability to identify rare susceptibility windows.
Brier Score: To assess the calibration of predicted probability of bacterial death against observed outcomes.
Fold-Change in Efficacy: Ratio of kill rate in 'predicted vulnerability window' vs. 'random timing' control.
Temporal Resolution Accuracy: Mean absolute error (in minutes) between predicted optimal intervention time and actual observed maximum susceptibility.
ablation: Sensor Resolution Ablation: Downsample metabolic data to 1-min, 5-min, and 15-min intervals to test the necessity of high-resolution monitoring.
Metabolic Marker Ablation: Remove specific markers (e.g., exclude membrane potential) to determine which metabolic dimensions are most predictive of vulnerability.
Strain-Specific Ablation: Test if models trained on one species generalize to another, testing the universality of the metabolic vulnerability mechanism.
experiments.validation_protocol: 5-fold cross-validation across different bacterial strains and experimental batches. External validation will be performed on a held-out set of 2 additional MDR strains not used in model training. Statistical significance of efficacy improvement will be tested using paired t-tests against the Random Timing Control.

baselines: Standard MIC Testing: Conventional broth microdilution to establish baseline static resistance profiles.
Random Timing Control: Antibiotic administration at random time points without metabolic guidance to establish average efficacy.
Constitutive Resistance Model: A null model assuming no temporal variation in susceptibility, predicting constant survival rates regardless of metabolic state.
metrics: Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC): To evaluate the classifier's ability to identify rare susceptibility windows.
Brier Score: To assess the calibration of predicted probability of bacterial death against observed outcomes.
Fold-Change in Efficacy: Ratio of kill rate in 'predicted vulnerability window' vs. 'random timing' control.
Temporal Resolution Accuracy: Mean absolute error (in minutes) between predicted optimal intervention time and actual observed maximum susceptibility.
ablation: Sensor Resolution Ablation: Downsample metabolic data to 1-min, 5-min, and 15-min intervals to test the necessity of high-resolution monitoring.
Metabolic Marker Ablation: Remove specific markers (e.g., exclude membrane potential) to determine which metabolic dimensions are most predictive of vulnerability.
Strain-Specific Ablation: Test if models trained on one species generalize to another, testing the universality of the metabolic vulnerability mechanism.
experiments.validation_protocol: 5-fold cross-validation across different bacterial strains and experimental batches. External validation will be performed on a held-out set of 2 additional MDR strains not used in model training. Statistical significance of efficacy improvement will be tested using paired t-tests against the Random Timing Control.
